statement: The efficacy tables analyze the efficacy population, the subjects with ADSL.EFFFL = Y, each in the column of the planned treatment ADSL.TRT01PN (0, 54, 81).

citations.quote: All patients who were randomized and took drug, and have at least 1 post-baseline measure
EFFFL="Y"

statement: The value of a subject at a week is the ADQSADAS record of the parameter ACTOT with that AVISIT and ANL01FL = Y: the assessment of the window that is closest to its target day, or, when the window has none, the last one carried forward (DTYPE = LOCF).

citations.quote: Missing postbaseline efficacy values will be imputed using last observation carried forward
the assessment closest to the target day will be selected
ANL01FL="Y" and AVISIT="Week 24"

statement: The ANCOVA of the change from baseline has the treatment and the pooled site group (SITEGR1) as factors and the baseline value (BASE) as a covariate, with no interaction. The documents disagree on the model of the dose-response test: the SAP and the code of the pairwise comparisons keep the baseline, the code of the dose-response test leaves it out. The value is the executor's reading, the one under which the CSR's numbers are reproduced; a person decides (PLAN.md section 4.5).

citations.quote: an ANCOVA model will be used with the baseline score, site, and treatment
a new pooled site identifier assigned for the purpose of analysis
will not assess site*treatment interaction
model CHG = trtpn sitegr1 base;
model CHG = trtpn sitegr1;

statement: The test of dose response is the test that the coefficient of the planned dose (0, 54, 81), a continuous variable in the ANCOVA, is 0.

citations.quote: H0: b = 0, where b is the coefficient for treatment
Treatment will be included as a continuous variable
randomized dose (0 for placebo; 54 for low dose; 81 for high dose)

statement: The pairwise comparisons are differences of LS means of the ANCOVA with the treatment as a factor: each dose against placebo and the high dose against the low dose, with the residual degrees of freedom, 95% confidence intervals and p-values not adjusted for multiple comparisons. They are shown whatever the test of dose response gives. The SAP's text performs them only when that test is significant, its template 5 shows them always; a person decides (PLAN.md section 4.5).

citations.quote: If the test for dose response is statistically significant, pairwise comparisons among the 3 groups will be performed
will only be performed if the test for dose response is significant
P-value(Xan - Placebo) [1][3]
p-values without adjustment for multiple comparisons
lsmeans trtpn / OM STDERR PDIFF CL

statement: LS means average over the pooled site groups with weights proportional to their numbers of model records (the observed margins).

citations.quote: lsmeans trtpn / OM STDERR PDIFF CL

statement: The rows Baseline summarize BASE on the records of the week of the table, so that Baseline, the week and the change describe the same subjects. No document says it; it is asked of the owner, and the build uses this value until the answer (the other reading, the baseline visit, gives the same cells on these data).

Numbers are shown with the decimals of SAP template 5: n 0, mean 1, SD 2, median 1, minimum and maximum 0, p-values 3, differences of LS means 1, their SE 2, the limits of their 95% CI 2; rounded half away from zero.
